current_example.problem:
Let $V = \mathbb{R}^3$ be the vector space equipped with the inner product

$$
\langle \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \rangle = 3 x_1 y_1 + x_2 y_2 + 2 x_3 y_3.
$$

Given that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216489/assets/0ab47976b1970f63246d1dc8d7232317ca30a479e771b34628f13b7688209477.svg) and ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14216489/assets/6b35ff9cc1cd68c1b150f6676bcffde6e0731dfb79a735a4004e71dabe044bcb.svg) are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ in $V,$ find the value of $k.$
current_example.worked_solution:
Since $\mathbf x$ and $\mathbf y$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =3{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+2{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =3\cdot (2\cdot k)+1\cdot (-2)+2\cdot (2\cdot (-1)) \\  & =6k-2-4 \\  & =6k-6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $\langle \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \rangle = 0$ and solve for $k\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =0 \\ 6k-6 & =0 \\ 6k & =6 \\ k & =1\end{aligned}
$$
